content.user_title: Convert Designs to FSD Tailwind Code
content.value_statement: Design handoff often breaks architecture, tokens, and accessibility. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to convert selected Figma or Pencil screens into layered Tailwind code.
actual_capabilities: Maps selected Figma or Pencil screens into Feature-Sliced Design layers.
Reconciles design variables with Tailwind CSS v4 @theme tokens.
Guides Server and Client component boundaries when the framework supports them.
Prioritizes existing project primitives before creating shared UI components.
Checks generated interfaces for states, keyboard access, labels, and contrast.
Uses project contracts and local architecture rules before applying defaults.
limitations: It needs access to selected design context, MCP output, or a local Pencil file.
The Pencil workflow is experimental and needs documented assumptions.
It does not replace repository architecture documents or design-system rules.
It cannot verify type checks, lint, or tests unless project commands are run.

use_cases.title: Build a Figma screen
use_cases.description: Convert one selected Figma frame into layered React UI with Tailwind CSS v4 tokens and accessible states.

use_cases.title: Align design tokens
use_cases.description: Compare Figma or Pencil variables against the existing token system before adding any new values.

use_cases.title: Refactor generated UI
use_cases.description: Split a monolithic generated component into shared, entities, features, widgets, pages, and app layers.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a selected frame
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert the selected Figma frame into React with Tailwind CSS v4. First list tokens, components, FSD layers, and accessibility states. Then implement only the selected frame and explain any assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Pencil screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill with the local Pencil file for one screen. Inspect variables, reusable components, layout direction, and assets. Produce a short plan, then generate layered Tailwind code that follows the project contract.

prompt_templates.title: Audit generated UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the generated UI against this skill. Check FSD import direction, token use, Server and Client boundaries, responsive assumptions, and accessibility states. Return only concrete issues and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor into project layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Take the existing single-component implementation and refactor it into the repository FSD structure. Reuse local primitives, preserve behavior, isolate client interactivity, and list any commands needed for validation.

output_examples.input: A selected Figma dashboard frame with a sidebar, item list, empty state, and primary action.
output: The response starts with a layer plan for app shell, page composition, widgets, features, entities, and shared primitives.
It identifies token mappings for surfaces, borders, text, radius, and brand actions.
It lists required states, including loading, empty, error, hover, focus-visible, disabled, and menu open.

output_examples.input: A Pencil file that contains one checkout screen and several reusable controls.
output: The response documents assumptions about responsive behavior because the design has one breakpoint.
It maps Pencil variables to existing Tailwind tokens before generating components.
It separates checkout actions into features and keeps route entries focused on composition.

output_examples.input: A generated component that mixes route logic, primitives, domain data, and interactive actions.
output: The response proposes a refactor that moves primitives to shared and domain display to entities.
It isolates action controls in features and composes the screen through widgets and pages.
It calls out validation steps for lint, type checks, tests, and manual keyboard review.

best_practices: Start from one selected frame, screen, or component instead of a whole design file.
Read the repository contract and component library before creating new primitives.
Map design variables to existing semantic tokens and document unresolved values.
anti_patterns: Do not translate a design into one large component without FSD decomposition.
Do not copy raw color or spacing values when token mappings exist.
Do not mark a whole page as client because one child is interactive.

faq.question: Does this skill require Figma MCP?
faq.answer: No. Figma MCP is preferred for Figma designs, but the skill can also use local Pencil files or provided design context.

faq.question: Can it convert an entire Figma file at once?
faq.answer: No. The workflow asks for one selected frame, screen, or component to keep the implementation accurate.

faq.question: Does it only work with React?
faq.answer: It is written for modern component-based frontend projects. React examples are primary, but the architecture rules can be adapted.

faq.question: How does it handle Tailwind CSS v3 projects?
faq.answer: It falls back to the project Tailwind v3 configuration and skips v4-only @theme guidance.

faq.question: Will it create new design tokens?
faq.answer: Only when the project contract or design system approves them. Otherwise it flags unmatched values for design review.

faq.question: What should be verified after generation?
faq.answer: Verify import direction, token use, accessibility states, responsive behavior, type checks, lint, and affected tests.
